# Shortlist

> Self-hosted, per-user movie and TV recommendations for Plex. Shortlist gives every user on a Plex
> server their own private "Picked for You" row on their Plex home screen, built from that person's
> own watch history and visible only to them. One Docker container, no AI key required.

Shortlist answers the question "can I give each of my Plex users recommendations based on what they
watched?" — which Plex itself does not do. Plex's built-in recommendation shelves are identical for
every account on the server.

## How the per-user privacy works

Plex has no per-user collections. It does have label restrictions: a collection is given a label, and
every *other* account's share filter gets `label!=<that label>` merged into it, leaving one account
able to see it. This requires Plex Media Server 1.43.2.10687 or newer — earlier versions ignore the
restriction on the Home and Recommended shelves.

The write ordering is the load-bearing part: rows are swept, delivered UNPROMOTED, the exclusions are
merged into every account's share filter, and only THEN are rows promoted onto Home. A row is
therefore never visible before the rule hiding it exists. Share filters are snapshotted before the
first change and restored exactly on uninstall.

## Key facts

- License: MIT. Free, no paid tier, nothing phones home.
- Requirements: Plex Media Server 1.43.2.10687+, Plex Pass on the admin account, a free TMDB API key.
- AI is OPTIONAL. The built-in picker needs no keys and no cloud. Supported optional providers:
  Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini, and any local OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama,
  llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, LocalAI).
- Every pick is verified to exist in the user's library before delivery — titles are never invented.
- Every pick carries a reason: "Because you watched X".
- Optional integrations: Tautulli, Radarr, Sonarr, Trakt, MDBList, Exa.
- Coexists with Kometa: only collections Shortlist created (labelled `shortlist_*`) are ever modified.
- Plex-only. There is no Jellyfin or Emby support, because the privacy model depends on Plex's
  label-based share filters.
- Status: 1.0, running in production.
